newsitem.title: UK: BA seeks EU block on French Air Liberte deal.
newsitem.headline: BA seeks EU block on French Air Liberte deal.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Friday it had asked Europe's Transport and Competition Commissioners to block "with utmost urgency" a bid by French regional airline AOM to buy its competitor Air Liberte, which is in receivership.
BA had said earlier in the day that it has itself expressed an interest in Air Liberte's assets.

"Allowing AOM to buy Air Liberte would be an illegal use of state aid," British Airways said in its letters, "because it would add further to the liabilities facing the AOM group, in contravention of the conditions of the Credit Lyonnais aid."
AOM is part of the distressed French bank group.

In a statement, BA said that it had explained to the commissioners that, if BA were to make a bid for Liberte, "this would be consistent with its efforts during the past three years to keep competition alive in France, through its French subsidiary TAT European Airlines".

TAT and AOM are not thought to be the only parties interested in Air Liberte, which BA says lost 650 million francs in the first nine months of this year and has total debts of about 1.5 billion francs.
According to French newspaper Le Monde, Britain's Virgin group is also sounding out the possibility of a bid.
According to French media reports, the country's largest carrier Air France is also a key player in the intrigue over how Liberte should be restructured.
Le Monde said on Friday that Paris wanted to create a second force around a new French airline based on a fusion of AOM, Air Liberte and privately-owned Euralair.

If BA were to buy Air Liberte, on the other hand, it would stand to gain a valuable toe-hold on slots at Paris Orly airport. "New slots at Orly are no longer available because of restrictions imposed by the French authorities," BA noted tersely in its statement.
